g.text: fraction of the task's own learning phase

rect.style: stroke-width: 1px; stroke: rgb(0, 0, 0); stroke-opacity: 0; fill: rgb(0, 0, 0); fill-opacity: 0;

text.style: font-family: Inter, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 9.5px; fill: rgb(108, 117, 125); fill-opacity: 1; white-space: pre;
text.tspan: Forward transfer is a ratio of the two shaded areas, eq. 9 of the CKA-RL paper:
(AUC − AUC​base​) / (1 − AUC​base​), where AUC is the mean normalised score over a task's own learning phase.
So AUC is the average height of these curves, and forward transfer is the share of the room the baseline left that the method takes.
x is normalised per method, because the metric averages each method over its own phase and those phases differ in length.
That is what the metric does, and it is also what it hides.
Four tasks, one per quarter of the sequence, chosen so their mean forward transfer reproduces each method's own:
Min-Max +0.13, CKA-RL +0.20, CReLUs +0.25 over all 50 tasks.
One seed (seed0), so these are real runs rather than an average of curves.
CbpNet (+0.18) and fine-tuning (+0.14) are omitted for space and sit between CKA-RL and CReLUs.
